# TODO5 — complete function-by-function reconstruction checklist

Inventory snapshot: 2026-09-14. This expands [Step 5 of TODO.md](TODO.md#5-reconstruct-the-program-subsystem-by-subsystem); it does not replace the overall project plan. Regenerate with `python3 tools/render_todo5.py` after updating the authoritative review records and analysis. Edit scope notes/grouping in that generator, not the generated rows. No original binary is read by this renderer.

## How to read this list

Every currently identified function has its own entry. Game routines are grouped by their original object module, under editorial subsystem headings. A module may mix UI and rules. Identity is keyed by **NE segment and entry offset**, never by spelling alone. Three final-byte zero-fill ranges are joined to their procedures, giving 846 functions rather than 849 coverage ranges. Addresses here are hexadecimal NE ordinals, not runtime selectors. All end offsets are exclusive; raw Ghidra addresses use a separate synthetic selector space.

- **[x] Reviewed source** means the whole original game procedure has reviewed, compiled C and the ledger’s original-instruction validation. It does not mean the full application or every native caller is integrated.
- **[ ] Partial** means a documented slice or caller-specific substitute exists; the whole procedure remains open.
- **[ ] Open** means no whole-function source credit is recorded; raw decompilation already exists and is a starting point.
- **[x] Library mapping** in the runtime appendix means the exported body lies within audited matching CRT code spans. It is not recovered runtime source, independent behavioral validation or final link integration.
- DOS-stub completion is counted separately. Neither CRT entries nor DOS entries inflate game-source coverage.

The source/evidence fields come from [coverage.json](analysis/coverage.json), maintained through [tracking/reviews.json](tracking/reviews.json). Some ledger validation strings still say native integration pending: recent package-level acceptance does not establish every function/caller combination. [START2A Windows 95 acceptance](analysis/compat/startup2a-win95.json) verifies the integrated title, wizard, colors and race roundtrip. It does not complete WinMain, world generation, game loading or turn processing.

**[x] Byte match** is separate evidence: native VC++ 1.52c generated every byte in the original function extent after resolving named address relocations into the original layout. No instruction bytes are masked or patched. This does not establish final executable linking or integration, and does not change the semantic-review ledger. See the [pilot](analysis/compat/byte-match.md) and [tutorial comparison](analysis/compat/tutorial-byte-match.md).

**25 functions / 5,791 bytes** have verified instruction byte matches. The renderer checks the evidence hashes against the current matching sources.

## Completion rules

For each open/partial entry, finish all of these before checking its main box:

1. Confirm original boundaries, debug signature, near/far ABI, DS/SS/ES assumptions, locals and embedded tables against the disassembly.
2. Resolve every basic block, direct/indirect call, callback, data reference and resource dependency. The calls listed below are the exported static graph, not a proof of all runtime dispatch.
3. Write readable, compilable source preserving widths, signedness, carry/wrap, shifts, pointer aliasing, x87 precision/rounding, RNG order, side effects and error/early-exit paths.
4. Compare normal and boundary/error cases against original instructions or documented native integration where appropriate. Check complete relevant state and service-call order, not just a return value.
5. Compile with the component; record evidence and exact scope in the review ledger. Native application integration remains a separate milestone where only a host semantic adapter exists.

**Per-entry detail:** “Signature” is the recovered effective debug description, not a host replacement prototype; `…` denotes no parameters recorded in that metadata, not a claim of variadic arguments. “Calls” includes every edge in the current exported graph, with duplicate call sites collapsed. “Callers” is a static count. Data-reference counts/labels are tool output and need semantic review; false labels are possible. Indirect-site notes are scoped by address to avoid merging same-named procedures. Module acceptance focus describes planned checks, not claims that those checks have already passed.

<a id="non-functions"></a>

## Work that a function list cannot mark complete

These obligations prevent “all names checked” from being mistaken for a full decompilation.

- [ ] **Original startup and final linking:** integrate every required subsystem under the recovered initialization/message/termination paths, without delegating work to the original executable or leaving milestone notices.
- [ ] **Complete native validation:** expand from START2A title/race acceptance to new/open/continue game, orders, turn generation, combat playback, reports, tutorial and error recovery.
- [ ] **CRT data:** close the __fptaskdata zero-slot transformation and common PAD/EPAD placement, plus the explicit unresolved audit items. Code-member identity alone does not close data/link layout.
- [ ] **Shared state/layout:** preserve globals, far-pointer representations, lifetime/ownership, zero-fill, tables and resource semantics across all callers.
- [ ] **Dispatch closure:** audit every callback, entry point, pointer table and unresolved indirect target using [indirect-targets.json](analysis/decompiler/indirect-targets.json), [code-pointers.json](analysis/decompiler/code-pointers.json) and [runtime-dispatch.json](analysis/decompiler/runtime-dispatch.json).
- [ ] **Uncovered ranges:** reconcile all non-procedure bytes with runtime code, embedded data, padding or genuinely missing functions. Do not invent one function per gap.
- [ ] **Resources:** all 122 payloads are already embedded, but full use/semantics across dialogs, strings, menus and commands remains open.
- [ ] **No-procedure modules:** retain debug/module records with no identified function bodies; an empty procedure list is not proof of no linked data or behavior.
- [ ] **Final evidence:** resolve behavior-affecting uncertainties and run whole-program comparisons; byte-identical linking remains the separate optional milestone in TODO.md.

## Keeping this inventory trustworthy

Update `tracking/reviews.json` and regenerate the coverage ledger using the existing project workflow before rerendering. Whole-function status is keyed by address, not just spelling. Update the generator’s partial-scope annotations when bounded implementations expand. The renderer asserts that all 846 game procedures join the 1,043-entry NE export exactly, all modules are categorized and every game signature is present. It preserves the old raw exports and does not change any reconstruction credit.
